names_note: **Fresh Air**, the room's pick (round 4 vote, unanimous: Wren's pick; Tomás moved from *The Right Size*, since Emerson's "no such thing as size" would contradict it for any guest who looks him up; Hester moved from *In Its Own Air*). It rests on Thoreau's November air and on what people feel after time with this guest. Also considered: *The Right Size* (Tomás), *In Its Own Air* (Hester), *Plenty*, *Out of Doors*, *Food for Walkers*, *To Be Eaten in the Wind*.
open_items: **The base is contested (card C1).** Oxford says the Stone Fence was "originally rum, and then whisky"; Jerry Thomas's 1862 drink is bourbon with sweet cider; the rum-and-hard-cider form is Wondrich's reading of the older drink. No 1750 recipe is on any page, so the pour says "the older way", never "the original recipe".

**Proportions owned (Tomás):** 45 ml rum to 120 ml cider sits between Oxford's "roughly equal portions" (22.8%, OUT of the highball band) and Thomas's glass filled up with cider; the guest text never calls it the colonial or Thomas's recipe.
**Emerson's words stay his (card C2, C3):** "chose to be rich by making his wants few" is used only as Emerson's line; ambition and "chose or fell into" are not stated as fact.
**Dates:** the page dates "Wild Apples" 1862 and the book 1863; the magazine and month are unverified (C4).
One web visit (Project Gutenberg, *Excursions*); everything else from the library. Veto-free; no new ingredient rows.
glassware: a heavy tumbler (about 300 ml), two or three small lumps of ice
name: Fresh Air
tagline: Nobody quite believes you when you say it's enough. It is.
epigraph: In 1862 a famous bar book printed this drink with sweet cider. Others kept pouring it tart.
